newsitem.title: USA: Article says FBI thought Jewell was gay cop-hater.
newsitem.headline: Article says FBI thought Jewell was gay cop-hater.

text.p: The FBI wasted weeks in its investigation of the Atlanta Olympics Park bombing pursuing an erroneous theory that security guard Richard Jewell was a gay cop-hater who had been assisted in the bombing by his lover, an article in Vanity Fair magazine said Tuesday.

The article portrays the FBI as hounding Jewell, who discovered the bomb that killed one person and injured 100 others, to the point where he thought that if he watched a television show in his home that showed a bombing, the federal agency would know and think the act suspicious.

"I kept thinking, these guys (the FBI) think I did this. These guys were accusing me of murder. This was the biggest case in the nation and the world. If they could pin it on me. they were going to put me in the electric chair," Jewell, who was cleared of involvement in the July 27 bombing, said in an extensive interview with Vantiy Fair.

The article, "American Nightmare: The Ballad of Richard Jewell" by Marie Brenner, quoted one of Jewell's lawyers, Jack Martin, as saying the FBI wasted weeks pursuing an erroneous theory that Jewell was a homosexual cop-hater who had been assisted in the bombing by his lover, who then made a warning call to police.
Brenner said the theory sprang from a rumour at a college where Jewell once worked as a campus policeman and where he had turned in several students for smoking marijuana.
